merger_description:
Schlumberger B.V. (**Schlumberger**), a direct wholly owned subsidiary of SLB N.V. (**SLB**), proposes to acquire 100% of the issued share capital, and sole control, of King TopCo Limited , the parent company of the Kelvion group (together with its subsidiaries, **Kelvion Group**), from King Holdings III, L.P. (the **Acquisition**).

SLB is a global technology company listed on the New York Stock Exchange, and together with its subsidiaries, comprises the **SLB Group**. The SLB Group primarily provides equipment, software and technical services, including subsurface evaluation, drilling and production services, to customers in the energy sector. It operates globally and focuses on decarbonisation, oil and gas, digital services and low-carbon energy technology solutions. SLB Group has recently expanded into the supply of modular data centre infrastructure.

The Kelvion Group is a global developer and manufacturer of thermal management technologies (that is, heat exchange and cooling solutions, including heat exchangers, evaporators, condensers, coolers and heat exchange coils) and is headquartered in Germany. These products are deployed across four key business segments:

1. ‘high tech’ end-markets (for example, data centres);
2. ‘conventional’ end-markets such as chemicals, transportation, heavy and light industry, food and beverage, heating, ventilation and air conditioning, and power and energy;
3. ‘green tech’ end-markets in the areas of liquefied natural gas, hydrogen renewable energy, heat pumps and carbon capture
4. repair and maintenance services and/or spare parts.

In Australia, the Kelvion Group supplies heat exchange and cooling products but does not have any local manufacturing capability.

determination_table_content.details:
In making this notification waiver determination, the Australian
Competition and Consumer Commission (the ACCC) has considered
the information provided with the notification waiver application and
had regard to the factors in section 51ABV(2)(b) of the Competition
and Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) (the Act).
Based on the information provided in the application, the ACCC
considers that the Acquisition is unlikely to give rise to any material
lessening of competition given:
a. there is no horizontal overlap or vertical relationship
between the SLB Group and the Kelvion Group in the supply
of modular infrastructure frameworks for data centre
applications and modular data centre infrastructure
solutions or the supply of heat exchange and cooling
products in Australia
b. there are numerous alternative suppliers of both modular
infrastructure frameworks for data centre applications and
modular data centre infrastructure solutions, as well as heat
exchange and cooling solutions in Australia and globally
c. there is a low risk of foreclosure or other concerning vertical
or conglomerate effects in Australia resulting from
exclusionary conduct, bundling or tying of products or
services post-acquisition.
In these circumstances, the ACCC does not consider it necessary to
reach a concluded view on the likelihood of the notification
thresholds being met.
Given that material competition concerns are unlikely to arise, the
ACCC has determined that the Acquisition is not required to be
notified.
The ACCC considers that the determination is consistent with the
object of the Act and the interests of consumers in promoting
competition.
For more information about the ACCC’s approach to considering
notification waiver applications and to assessing competition
effects more generally, see the ACCC’s guidance on notification
waivers and merger assessment guidelines.
